caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2028 of 2015
lawyer:
Abdus Salam Mondal, DAG, instructed by Shirin Afroz, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
None represented ----- Respondents.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Abdul Barek Bepari and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 2-5-2013, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2252 of 2008 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 6-4-2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal, in Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2007 under Order XLI, rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for re-admitting the appeal to its original file and number. 

 That the respondents No.1 to 94 herein instituted Title Suit No. 46 of 1997 in the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge, Barisal, praying for declaration of title, which was decreed on contest. Against the same the present petitioner as appellant preferred Title Appeal No. 57 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge, Barisal which was ultimately transferred to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal. On 15-2-2007 when the appeal was taken up for hearing no one was found present on behalf of the appellant and, as such, the same was dismissed for default. Subsequently on 20-3-2007 the appellant petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2007 under Order XLI, rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for readmission of the appeal. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Barisal upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the application allowed the said miscellaneous case and set aside the order of dismissal of the appeal for default and re-admitted the same to its original file and number by order dated 6-4-2008. 

 6. Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the Government, petitioner submits that the High Court Division erred in law in construing the application for re-admission of the appeal under Order XLI, rule 19A of the Code which actually was filed under Order XLI, rule 19 of the Code and, as such, committed error of law in holding that the Court of appeal below committed gross illegality in allowing the application for re-admission of the appeal which was filed beyond the statutory period of 30 days limitation. He submits that the appeal was dismissed for default on 15-2-2007 and the Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2007 was filed for re-admission of the same on 20-3-2007, after obtaining the certified copy within time, with explanation but the High Court Division did not consider the explanation of the appellant and, as such, by passing the impugned judgment and order the appellant government has been debarred from persuading its appeal, which was dismissed for default, for no fault on its part. 

 8. On perusal of the materials on record it appears that the appeal was preferred by the Government appellant challenging the judgment and decree of the trial court. But unfortunately the appeal was dismissed for default on 15-2-2007 for which the said miscellaneous case was filed on 20-3-2007 for re-admission of the appeal. On perusal of the application for re-admission of the appeal it appears that the same has been filed under Order XLI Rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code with following prayers: 

 11. As it has already been stated above that the appeal was dismissed for default on 15-2-2007 and after obtaining the certified copy of the dismissal order, the application for re-admission of the appeal was filed on 20-3-2007 supported by verification. Under Rule 19 section 5 of the Limitation Act applies as such even if the application is filed out of time the same can be considered if there are good and satisfactory grounds for condonation of delay and allowing the application. So unless the aforesaid two conditions embodied in the 1st proviso of Rule 19A are met the same may not be invoked. In that case the Court can deal with the matter under Rule 19. It should be kept in mind that re-admission of appeal under Rule 19 is a discretionary power of the court and the settled principle of law is discretion to be exercised in a judicious manner having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case (Surendra Nath Sarkar vs Md Jalil Shaikh reported in 3 MLR (AD) 98 and Salamat Bibi vs Settlement and Rehabilitation Commissioner, Multan reported in 21 DLR (SC) 353). Only distinction between Rule 19 and 19A is filing of the application for re-admission within 30 days and by affidavit. Other than this under both the provisions, the appeal may be re-admitted on payment of costs. In the present case the Court of appeal below while re-admitting the appeal imposed cost of Taka 1000 and the appellant having complied with the requirement of law the court of appeal below has re-admitted the appeal upon setting aside its earlier order of dismissal for default of the appeal. 

 12. But the High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment and order under the revisional jurisdiction held "the application has not been filed within 30 days from the date of dismissal order nor it was supported by any affidavit" and hence the High Court Division found that the Court of appeal below committed illegality in passing the order of re-admission. The High court Division also misconstrued the application for re-admission of the appeal as an application filed under Order XLI, rule 19A but without any affidavit, but failed to consider that the same has been actually filed under Order XLI, rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code supported by verification and erroneously came to a conclusion that the application has not been filed within 30 days nor supported by an affidavit. This approach of the High Court Division is erroneous as Rule 19A has not spelt out that in absence of the said two conditions the application shall be rejected. Rather under such circumstances the same should be dealt with under Order XLI, rule 19 which does not require to be filed by swearing affidavit. In this score also, the High Court Division committed illegality in passing the impugned judgment. 

 13. The Limitation Act provides filing of appeal or any application challenging any decree or order, whatsoever, of the court upon obtaining the certified copy of the same and section 12(2) of the Limitation Act provides that the time consumed in obtaining such copy shall be excluded. In the instant case, it appears that neither there is any statement as to delay or there is any prayer for condonation of delay nor there is any such finding by the court of appeal below. As such it can be safely construed that the application was filed within time. So there was no bar in allowing the application. As such Rule 19 is very much applicable in the present case. Hence we hold that the High Court Division committed error of law in not taking the above facts into consideration and, as such, came an erroneous finding that the re-admission was made without complying with the provision of law. 

 14. Moreover, the intention of the legislature in enacting Rule 19A is to avoid delay in re-admitting the appeal and to expedite disposal of the same. But when the criterion of Rule 19A is not fulfilled Rule 19 will be invoked which has not been totally ousted. In this case, the court of appeal below upon considering all materials on record readmitted the appeal on imposing cost of Taka 1000 and, as such, rightly allowed the miscellaneous case and readmitted the appeal.
